title: Genghis Khan and the Mongol World

cards.h: An orphan on the run built the largest land empire ever
cards.b:
The boy was called Temüjin. Born around 1162, he saw his father poisoned when he was a child. His family was left to starve on the steppe.

He grew up to unite every Mongol tribe and in 1206 was named Genghis Khan ('Chinggis', a title whose exact meaning is debated).

Temüjin survived by wits. His wife Börte was kidnapped and he rescued her. He used loyal friends rather than only family.

His army was divided into groups of ten, hundred, thousand. Promotions went to the skilled, not just nobles. In 1206, a kurultai (assembly) proclaimed him ruler.

Mongol armies were fast horse-archers who could ride very long distances. They used spies and tricks. Cities that fought could be wiped out. The Khwarazmian empire (Central Asia, 1219-1221) was ruined after its governor killed Mongol envoys or traders.

Genghis died in 1227, while fighting Western Xia. His burial place has never been found.

His grandson Batu reached Hungary in 1241, then withdrew when Great Khan Ogedei died (the exact reason is debated). Kublai Khan took all China and founded the Yuan dynasty in 1271. Hulagu took Baghdad in 1258.

The Mongols protected trade routes. A relay system, the yam, with riders and stations, carried messages. Travellers with a metal pass (paiza) got food and horses. This 'Pax Mongolica' let Marco Polo and others travel.

The Mongols were mostly tolerant of religions, though they could be cruel.

By the late 1200s the empire had split into four khanates. Yuan China fell in 1368. The Golden Horde ruled Russia for generations.

At its peak the empire covered about 24 million square km, the biggest contiguous land empire in history.

Persian and Chinese sources describe massacres, with huge figures (sometimes millions) that modern historians doubt as exaggerated.

A famous 2003 study found a Y-chromosome line shared by about 8 percent of men in a big region of Asia. It is linked to a single male ancestor around 1,000 years ago. Some say it may be Genghis Khan's family, but this is a guess and scholars are cautious.

Five things to remember

  1. Genghis Khan was proclaimed ruler in 1206.
  2. His army used merit, speed and discipline.
  3. The empire split into khanates among his heirs.
  4. The yam relay and the Pax Mongolica helped trade.
  5. Mongols turned back at the Indus in 1221.

Think about it

  • Should an empire be judged by its builders or its victims?
  • Why would tolerance for religions help a conquering state?
